newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 3.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Treasury bond prices fell more than a point on signs of a stronger economy.
- Manufacturing gained steam last month, putting in its best showing since June.
- Ameritech became the first Baby Bell to ask regulators for permission to offer long distance services.
- Bank of New York plans to double its stake in State Street Boston to just under 10 percent.
- CompUSA said its comparable store sales rose by only 1.5 percent in the last quarter of 1996.
- Microsoft has gone on a buying binge to capture new markets, undercut competitors and supply some of the new revenue the software giant needs to maintain its furious growth rate.
- East Coast ports are slashing rates up to 30 percent in a drive to regain market share.
- Conrail and Union Pacific won a major victory in a freight hauling case before federal regulators.
- Hollywood ticket sales rose 10 percent to a record $5.8 billion.
- The general counsel of the NASD's regulatory arm says he still expects charges to emerge from the group's four-year inquiry into the municipal bond business.
- Rexene said it won't oppose any future buyout offer for $16 per share as long as certain criteria are met.
- Holiday retail sales may be on a permanent decline in the wake of yet another disappointing season for most retailers.
- Tool maker Stanley Works named John Trani, a General Electric executive, chairman and chief executive officer.
- Abbott Labs settled deceptive advertising charges brought by the FTC by backing off the use of endorsements from doctors for its Ensure beverage.
